label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IV.7, 1011b23-24: Excluded middle as a general principle: every proposition…
interpretation: Ontic reading of 'there cannot be anything between the two sides of a contradiction; of one subject one must either affirm or deny any one predicate', read with the definition of truth that follows (1011b25-29: to say of what is that it is, or of what is not that it is not, is true). The 'must' is taken as a thesis about how things are, so that one of the two assertions is true, not as a claim about what a speaker must actually utter. Aristotle states the law for predication ('one of one'); the propositional form over all propositions is constructively equivalent to the predicative form over all subjects and predicates (TruthCore.Logic.excludedMiddle_iff_predicative), so it does not strengthen the passage. Aristotle offers no demonstration here: the chapter argues for the law against its deniers.
